# go.exe builds a binary named after its package or at `output`, passes
# `flags` to go build, rebuilds when a Go source it imports or an extra input
# changes but not for an unrelated package, and --clean removes the binary.
[!exec:go] skip

bit
stdout 'hello ▶ go build -o hello -trimpath \./cmd/hello'
stdout 'stamped ▶ go build -o bin/stamped -trimpath -ldflags=-X main\.version=1\.2\.3 \./cmd/hello'
exec ./hello
stdout '\Ahello dev\n\z'
exec ./bin/stamped
stdout '\Ahello 1\.2\.3\n\z'

bit
stdout 'hello · no changes'
stdout 'stamped · no changes'

# A package outside the binary's imports changes nothing.
cp other.go.changed other/other.go
bit
! stdout '▶'

# A package the binary imports rebuilds both.
cp greet.go.changed greet/greet.go
bit
stdout 'hello ▶ go build .*\(''greet/greet\.go'' changed\)'
stdout 'stamped ▶ go build .*\(''greet/greet\.go'' changed\)'
exec ./hello
stdout '\Ahi dev\n\z'

# Extra inputs rebuild only the target that names them.
cp asset.txt.changed assets/logo.txt
bit
stdout 'stamped ▶ go build .*\(''assets/logo\.txt'' changed\)'
! stdout 'hello ▶'

bit --clean
! exists hello
! exists bin/stamped

# `-o` belongs in `output`.
cp BUILD.bit.output-flag BUILD.bit
! bit
stderr '`flags` must not contain `-o`: set `output` instead'

-- BUILD.bit --
hello = go.exe {
  package = "./cmd/hello"
}

stamped = go.exe {
  package = "./cmd/hello"
  output  = "bin/stamped"
  flags   = ["-ldflags=-X main.version=1.2.3"]
  inputs  = ["assets/*.txt"]
}
-- BUILD.bit.output-flag --
hello = go.exe {
  package = "./cmd/hello"
  flags   = ["-o=elsewhere"]
}
-- go.mod --
module example.com/m

go 1.22
-- cmd/hello/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"example.com/m/greet"
)

var version = "dev"

func main() { fmt.Println(greet.Word, version) }
-- greet/greet.go --
package greet

const Word = "hello"
-- greet.go.changed --
package greet

const Word = "hi"
-- other/other.go --
package other
-- other.go.changed --
package other

const X = 1
-- assets/logo.txt --
logo
-- asset.txt.changed --
new logo
